headline: Bitcoin is holding around $60,000 after Saturday's crash to its lowest price in about two years, while money keeps leaving US bitcoin funds and traders expect the Fed to raise rates in December.

market.asOf: Read by this desk on Sat 21 Nov at about 19:57-19:58 UTC (02:57 Sun Bangkok) from CoinMarketCap. CoinGecko's pages showed much higher ether and solana prices that did not match CoinMarketCap or other Saturday reports, so they were not used. Prices move fast; use the live prices on this page.
market.fearGreed: 12 out of 100, "Extreme Fear", on the Alternative.me Crypto Fear & Greed Index (read at about 19:57 UTC), the same as the day before.

stories.title: Bitcoin holds near $60,000 after its lowest price in two years
stories.summary: Bitcoin fell to its lowest price in about two years early on Saturday, then bounced back to around $60,000. Traders who had borrowed to bet were forced out in a big wave, and many holders are now sitting on losses.
points: Bitcoin fell as low as $55,251.60, its lowest level in two years, per Reuters.
Bitcoin briefly rose above $60,000 around 13:30 GMT and was later up more than 8% at about $59,952, per Reuters.
About $2.67 billion of crypto bets were liquidated over 24 hours, per CoinGlass data cited by Bitcoin.com News.
Money held in bitcoin at a loss reached about $950 billion, the highest on record, per analyst Darkfost cited by crypto.news.

sources.label: Reuters via AOL: bitcoin falls to two-year low
Bitcoin.com News: rebound to $60K after crash near $55K

stories.title: US bitcoin funds keep losing money; November outflows near $3.6 billion
stories.summary: Money kept flowing out of US spot bitcoin ETFs, the funds that let people buy bitcoin through a normal brokerage account. Friday's outflow was much smaller than Thursday's, but BlackRock's fund had still not posted its Friday number.
points: Friday 20 Nov's provisional total was -$124.5 million, with BlackRock's IBIT still unpublished, per CryptoTicker using Farside data.
On Thursday 19 Nov IBIT lost $541.1 million, its biggest one-day withdrawal since launch, per CryptoTicker.
November outflows total about $3.59 billion including Friday's provisional figure, per CryptoTicker.
Bitcoin ETFs lost about $1.25 billion over 16-20 Nov and ether ETFs about $221.7 million, per crypto.news.

stories.title: Stock market correction and Fed hike fears weigh on crypto
stories.summary: Friday's AI-led sell-off pushed the S&P 500 and Dow into a correction, meaning more than 10% below their record highs, and crypto company shares fell with them. Markets also expect the Fed to raise interest rates in December. US stocks are closed for the weekend, so Monday's open is the next test.
points: On Friday the S&P 500 fell 3.70%, its seventh straight daily loss, the Dow 1.93% and the Nasdaq 5.28%, per Reuters.
Nvidia fell 13.8%, and Coinbase, Strategy and Robinhood fell between 6.3% and 9.6%, per Reuters.
Markets see a near-certain quarter-point Fed rate hike in December, per Reuters citing CME FedWatch.
Reuters says bitcoin is increasingly moving in step with stocks.

sources.label: Reuters via Yahoo Finance: Friday's stock market close
Reuters via AOL: bitcoin falls to two-year low

briefs.title: Kraken Canadian-dollar price glitch
briefs.summary: Bitcoin briefly traded as low as C$24,250 on Kraken's Canadian-dollar market, about 71% below the market price; the cause is still unclear and the trades are yet to be verified, per U.Today.

briefs.title: Senate passes bill on war and death bets
briefs.summary: The Senate passed a bill to bar federally registered exchanges from listing prediction-market contracts on war, terrorism, assassination or death; it now goes to the House, per CoinDesk.

briefs.title: MoonPay applies for a US trust bank charter
briefs.summary: MoonPay applied to the OCC, a US bank regulator, for a national trust bank charter covering stablecoin issuance, redemption and custody, per Cointelegraph.

briefs.title: Binance hack funds moving through mixers
briefs.summary: Elliptic says about 2,310 BTC (about $149 million) from the Binance hack has gone through coinjoin mixers, per The Block.

briefs.title: XRP slips below $1
briefs.summary: XRP traded near $0.87, about 9% lower than a day earlier, with most of about $18 million in liquidated futures being bets on higher prices, per The Crypto Basic.

briefs.title: JPMorgan: bitcoin trades far below its mining cost
briefs.summary: JPMorgan estimates it costs about $86,000 to produce one bitcoin, which squeezes higher-cost miners, per The Block.

Remarks on the economic outlook and monetary policy, with Q&A, per the New York Fed.
October came in at 91.7 against 81 expected, per Newsquawk.

calendar.event: Dell, HP Inc and Workday earnings
calendar.note: Dell is watched as a gauge of AI server demand after Friday's AI stock rout; analysts expect revenue of about $50.6 billion, per Finviz. Dates from earnings calendars, not company sites.

calendar.event: US PCE inflation (Oct), Q3 GDP (second estimate), durable goods and jobless claims
calendar.note: PCE and Q3 GDP are both due at 8:30am ET, per the BEA schedule. Core PCE is expected at 3.2% a year (prior 3.1%), per Newsquawk. Q3 GDP is expected at 3.5% per Trading Economics, against the 3.4% first estimate. Weekly jobless claims (last 203K) move to Wednesday for the holiday, per Newsquawk.
The Fed's survey of business conditions around the country, per the Fed's calendar. October new home sales come out earlier the same day at 10:00am ET (22:00 Bangkok), per the Census Bureau.
On Friday 27 Nov US stocks close early at 1:00pm ET (01:00 Sat Bangkok), per NYSE. Crypto trades all day, but thin trading can mean bigger swings.

calendar.event: Monthly bitcoin and ether options expiry on Deribit
calendar.note: KCEX's blog put the bitcoin expiry at about $6.5 billion with the "max pain" level at $75,000 (written 17 Nov, before this week's fall).
Fed officials stop public comment on policy from 28 Nov through 10 Dec, per the Fed's blackout calendar.
The last jobs report before the Fed decision, per the BLS schedule. JOLTS job openings come out Tue 1 Dec at 10:00am ET (22:00 Bangkok); November CPI is Thu 10 Dec, the day after the Fed.

calendar.event: Next Fed meeting and rate decision
calendar.note: Two-day meeting 8-9 Dec with new economic projections, per the Fed's calendar. The current range is 3.75-4.00%, held on 28 Oct with two officials voting for a hike, per the Fed. Markets expect a quarter-point hike.
